extracted.intended_audience: startup founders / early-stage CEOs doing press and media outreach
extracted.subtask_description: Practical playbook for founders on when to pursue PR, how to pitch reporters, what story angles work, common mistakes to avoid, and a short email template and quality checklist for founder-led media outreach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Build asymmetric trust before scale
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Benefit: PR creates credibility early that helps talent, customers, and investors trust you before your company is large. Use PR strategically to establish reputation ahead of growth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create inbound pipeline via PR
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Benefit: Good coverage should generate inbound interest across recruiting, sales, and fundraising — think of coverage as a persistent channel, not one-off vanity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Differentiate in a crowded market
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Benefit: PR can help your story stand out from competitors; focus on distinctive angles rather than generic product claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use PR as social proof for cold outreach
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides social proof for cold outreach
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Benefit: Media coverage can be cited in outbound messages to improve response rates; aim for credible outlets and truthful claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid PR before product-market fit
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When NOT to do PR: If you haven't validated PMF, avoid PR because coverage can amplify flaws and attract premature scrutiny or expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid PR when you don't want competitor attention
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When NOT to do PR: If publicity would draw harmful competitive responses (e.g., copycats or hostile moves), delay coverage until defensibility is stronger.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stay stealth if legitimate reasons exist
rubrics_metrics.description: You're in stealth for legitimate reasons
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When NOT to do PR: If your strategy or product requires secrecy (legal, competitive, or partnership considerations), maintain stealth rather than seeking press.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't do PR if your product doesn't work yet
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When NOT to do PR: Avoid publicizing while the product is broken; bad early impressions are sticky and reporters/ customers will remember.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid PR if your story isn't differentiated
rubrics_metrics.description: Your story isn't different from competitors
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When NOT to do PR: If your narrative is indistinguishable from others, coverage is unlikely and may harm credibility. Find a unique angle first.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be your own PR person initially
rubrics_metrics.description: Be your own PR person at first — no agency until $5M ARR
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: Founders should handle early media outreach themselves to save money and build relationships; outsource to agencies only after reaching significant scale (e.g., ~$5M ARR).

rubrics_metrics.name: Build reporter relationships before need
rubrics_metrics.description: Build relationships with 10-20 reporters BEFORE you need coverage
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: Proactively cultivate a small network of reporters you can call on; aim for depth of relationships rather than broad, cold outreach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offer exclusives instead of mass-blasting
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: Give one reporter an exclusive to increase interest and perceived value; avoid blasting the same pitch to many reporters simultaneously.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tell the truth / avoid embellishment
rubrics_metrics.description: Tell the truth — embellishment kills you in 6 months
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: Be honest in claims and numbers — exaggeration leads to loss of credibility and long-term harm with press and stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't overhype — reporters remember restraint
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporters remember founders who DIDN'T overhype
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: Avoid hype language; measured, factual storytelling builds long-term reporter trust and better outcomes for repeat coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Founder email subject convention
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: Keep subject lines clear and specific (news + founder + company) so reporters immediately understand relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Founder email — paragraph 1 (one-sentence news)
rubrics_metrics.description: Para 1: The news in one sentence
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: Lead with the single most important fact; be concise and avoid burying the lede.

rubrics_metrics.name: Founder email — paragraph 2 (why it matters)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: Provide the significance or context that explains relevance to the reporter's audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Founder email — paragraph 3 (offer)
rubrics_metrics.description: Para 3: What I can offer (call, exclusive, demo)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: State concretely what access you’re offering — interviews, exclusive data, demos — to make it easy for the reporter to act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Founder email — sign-off and length
rubrics_metrics.description: Sign off with phone number; Total: under 150 words
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: Always include a phone number for quick access and keep the entire email under ~150 words to respect reporters' time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counter-intuitive market insight angle
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Story angle: Reporters like surprising, evidence-backed insights that change conventional wisdom; present data or a clear rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Big-name customer/partner reveal angle
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Story angle: Announcing a well-known customer or partner provides credibility and newsworthiness; get permission and quotes if required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honest pivot narrative
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Story angle: A candid pivot that highlights lessons learned can be compelling; avoid spin and emphasize concrete changes and outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: High-profile hiring announcement (qualified)
rubrics_metrics.description: Hiring announcement (only if person is famous)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Story angle: Only pitch hires when the person has notable recognition or relevance; otherwise hiring news is low-value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding announcement requirements
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Story angle: Funding news is most newsworthy at Series A and above and is stronger when named investors are included; earlier raises are less likely to attract coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proprietary data report angle
rubrics_metrics.description: Data report from your unique data set
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Story angle: Publishable, proprietary data or trends derived from unique datasets can be a strong PR asset — present clear methodology and interpretability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mistake — hiring agency too early
rubrics_metrics.description: Hiring expensive PR agency too early
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-pattern: Founders often waste money on agencies before they understand their story or have traction; DIY early to learn what works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mistake — vague 'coverage' asks
rubrics_metrics.description: Asking for 'coverage' generally, not pitching specific story
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-pattern: Don't ask for generic coverage; pitch a specific, reporter-relevant story or exclusive to increase chances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mistake — following up too aggressively
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-pattern: Excessive follow-ups annoy reporters and burn relationships; follow up judiciously and respectfully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mistake — burning embargo
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-pattern: Respect embargoes; leaking or breaking agreed timing damages trust with journalists and outlets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mistake — lying or exaggerating numbers
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-pattern: Fabricated or inflated metrics will be discovered and ruin credibility; always use honest, verifiable numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mistake — pitching same reporter same story repeatedly
rubrics_metrics.description: Pitching the same reporter the same story repeatedly
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-pattern: Repeating identical pitches signals laziness and erodes relationships; tailor and evolve your story or change targets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality: real news worth telling
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quality rubric: The story must be genuinely newsworthy — not incremental fluff — to merit reporter time and audience attention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality: personalized pitch
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quality rubric: Pitches must be tailored to the reporter and outlet instead of mass emails; show familiarity with the reporter's beat.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality: founder voice
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quality rubric: Write in authentic founder language rather than marketing or agency-speak; authenticity is memorable for reporters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality: honest numbers
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quality rubric: Provide accurate, defensible metrics and be prepared to back them up; avoid rounded or unverifiable claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality: offer exclusive first
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quality rubric: Offer an exclusive to one reporter/outlet first to increase pickup and build relationships; avoid immediate mass distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality: phone number provided
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quality rubric: Include a phone number in outreach so reporters can quickly reach you for clarifications or interviews.
